extra-001: The Boolean transition does not specify the internal node's initial charge.
With B already on, the internal node starts near ground, reducing charge that must be removed.
The initially charged internal node adds charge to the discharge event; it does not make it faster in this model.
A falling NAND output is discharged through the nMOS stack, not driven down by the pMOS network.
extra-002: Widening also increases input and diffusion capacitance.
The stated external load is fixed; widening the driver does not halve it.
Reduced resistance trades against larger self-loading and the load presented to preceding stages.
Parasitic delay and upstream loading prevent a universal factor-of-two path improvement.
extra-003: With capture-minus-launch skew, setup contains +s and same-edge hold contains −s.
A later capture edge extends the old-data hold requirement, worsening hold.
This reverses the explicitly stated skew convention.
A shared clock source does not eliminate different clock arrival times.
extra-004: Clock period changes the next-cycle setup budget, not this unchanged same-edge hold race.
Capture setup time is a different timing constraint.
Added minimum data delay directly postpones the new arrival; its maximum delay must also fit setup.
Removing data buffers generally shortens the already too-fast path.
extra-005: A pull-up keeper opposes, rather than directly strengthens, the selected pull-down current.
Restoration protects a high bitline but reduces net current during a legitimate falling read.
A keeper supplies restoration current; it does not disconnect bitline capacitance.
The next access still needs a defined precharge state.
extra-006: A stronger keeper can mask some noise while slowing valid reads; it does not guarantee hazard-free selection.
Unequal address arrival can activate an unintended wordline; settling and selection control prevent the erroneous discharge.
Removing precharge retains stale state rather than establishing a fresh evaluation.
A slower output inverter does not prevent the dynamic bitline from losing charge.
extra-007: This reverses the usual access-strength tradeoff under the stated fixed pull-up/pull-down sizing.
Improved write authority does not imply improved read stability.
Stronger access helps overwrite the cell but also couples the high read bitline more strongly into its stored-zero node.
In hold, the access devices are off; changing their width does not automatically destroy bistability.
extra-008: Regenerative gain amplifies the initial effective sign, which can be wrong.
The unfavorable 25 mV offset exceeds the 15 mV signal, so more gain alone cannot guarantee the desired decision.
Mismatch creates offset; gain does not cancel it.
Common mode affects operation, but the differential signal and offset determine the decision polarity.
extra-009: B·C = 1 forces Y low and blocks the A arc.
B·C = 0 reduces the expression to Y = NOT(A), sensitizing A to Y.
Multiple simultaneous input transitions do not isolate the A propagation arc.
Holding A fixed cannot measure the A-to-Y transition delay.
extra-010: Monotonicity is a useful QA expectation, not sufficient grounds to delete an unexplained result.
Smoothing can hide an extraction error or a real nonlinear feature.
Waveforms and run conditions reveal wrong crossing selection, incomplete settling or convergence problems before any repair.
Resizing changes the experiment without explaining the suspect measurement.
extra-011: Timing values are referenced to external crossings, so a small negative setup can be valid.
Internal clock latency can permit slightly later data while meeting the documented output-delay criterion.
A negative setup number does not remove the independent hold constraint.
A finite internal transparency window does not mean the latch remains open indefinitely.
extra-012: DRC checks geometry independently of LVS connectivity.
Extracted parasitics can change delay even when connectivity matches.
LVS supports a connectivity claim; geometry, parasitics, performance and integration need separate evidence.
Pin accessibility is a routing/integration property, not an LVS guarantee.
extra-013: Finger count can change physical parasitics without changing the inverter truth table.
Diffusion sharing and contact/gate/metal routing change the extracted electrical network.
Equal total channel width does not specify equal diffusion geometry or routing.
More fingers may reduce some diffusion terms while adding routing or contact costs.
extra-014: DC average current misses the transient demand coincident with precharge.
Local resistive and inductive droop depend on the current waveform and available charge support.
The timing of the failure motivates checking supply dynamics before assigning an unrelated cause.
Removing charge support can worsen droop; decap placement and resonance should be evaluated instead.
extra-015: Average current alone omits heating and any applicable peak constraints.
Peak current alone discards duty-cycle and thermal information.
Directional average, RMS heating and peak stresses must be assessed under the applicable process methodology.
Pulsed current can still cause material transport and Joule heating.
extra-016: A low gate with the pMOS source near VDD produces negative VGS; temperature and duty factor matter for BTI stress.
The stated long static interval motivates a static-bias mechanism, not only switching-related NMOS stress.
Static bias can maintain electric-field stress and cause aging.
A static voltage across an oxide still creates an electric field.
extra-017: Changing enable during clock high can add a rising edge or shorten the active pulse.
An AND output follows changes on enable while the clock is high.
Unintended clock edges can change sequential state, so the concern is functional as well as energetic.
Clock gating introduces gating checks and does not remove downstream data timing requirements.
extra-018: This demands a higher frequency before voltage supports it, and removes voltage before lowering the demand.
Raising settled voltage first and reducing frequency first keeps operation within the supported voltage/frequency envelope.
Safe transient operation depends on the instantaneous voltage/frequency pair, not just average power.
A lower voltage can fail the unchanged frequency requirement.
extra-019: The sum contains twice the common additive global term.
Subtracting equal-sensitivity delays cancels the same additive global contribution while retaining local mismatch.
A common additive shift also shifts the maximum.
Independent local mismatch terms remain after common-mode cancellation.
extra-020: No observed failures in a small sample does not demonstrate a rare-event target.
Zero observations do not establish zero true probability.
For 100 independent trials and zero failures, the one-sided 95% upper bound is about 2.95%, far above one in a million.
A sample maximum has no automatic six-sigma interpretation.
extra-021: Synchronizers reduce propagation risk per bit; they do not make a multi-bit transfer atomic.
Different synchronization latencies can combine bits from different transmitted words.
Two-flop synchronization can be used between unrelated frequencies when the signal protocol is appropriate.
A faster destination clock alone does not enforce coherent multi-bit capture.
extra-022: Appearance alone does not establish numerical convergence or physical correctness.
Convergence, time resolution and measurement identity must stabilize before interpreting the waveform.
Adding load changes the circuit and can mask the symptom without explaining it.
Time discretization, output compression and nonlinear solver behavior affect transient measurements.
extra-023: Zero-filling turns a failed measurement into an apparently excellent delay.
Silent omission hides missing sweep coverage.
Explicit status, units and completeness retain the evidence needed to distinguish valid data from failed runs.
Alphabetical string order does not compare normalized physical delay values.
extra-024: Hot is not universally slow near threshold; threshold and mobility trends compete.
Discarding an unexplained slow corner can hide a real failure.
Validate the corner and investigate whether cold threshold increase outweighs improved mobility at this voltage.
Reducing supply does not universally improve speed and can worsen near-threshold delay.
platform-analog-differential-pair-polari: The stated differential output is drain 2 minus drain 1, giving positive gain; a single branch also carries the factor of one-half.
Each branch changes by ±gm·vid/2, giving −2.5 V/V at drain 1 and +5 V/V differentially.
This interchanges the single-ended/differential magnitudes and gives the wrong drain-1 sign.
A fixed total tail current permits equal and opposite incremental branch currents.
platform-analog-current-mirrors-diagnosi: A repeatable voltage-dependent knee first calls for checking operating region, not merely averaging random mismatch.
Changing the intended ratio does not restore saturation at insufficient output voltage.
Insufficient VDS can move the output device out of saturation and collapse the mirrored current.
A cascode can improve output resistance while increasing the minimum output-voltage requirement.
platform-analog-noise-offset-offset: Independent zero-mean scatter averages down; a constant bias remains.
Independent noise standard error scales as 1/√N, and a constant offset does not average away.
A constant voltage bias is not a noise spectral density.
Narrower bandwidth can reduce integrated noise without removing DC offset.
platform-analog-sampling-adc-alias: More resolution represents the already aliased samples more accurately without disambiguating their origin.
Averaging that preserves the occupied band cannot separate the interferer from the overlapping signal.
Analog rejection before sampling removes the out-of-band interferer before irreversible spectral overlap.
The deterministic interferer is not made harmless by treating it as quantization noise.
platform-rtl-sequential-semantics-pipeli: This incorrectly propagates newly updated a into b at the same edge.
Both right-hand sides use the pre-update state: a receives din=1 and b receives old a=0.
This swaps the values assigned by the stated right-hand sides.
The initial values and input are explicitly known, so the update is determinate.
platform-rtl-cdc-handshake-reuse: The destination may not yet have captured the payload when request is asserted.
A fixed source-cycle wait does not establish destination receipt across unrelated clocks.
Safely returned acknowledgement and the defined protocol completion establish when the current payload may be replaced.
A clean-looking simulation does not prove coherent transfer or completion of the handshake.
platform-rtl-reset-verification-valid: An incidental simulator initialization does not establish hardware startup behavior.
Datapath width does not prevent use of uninitialized data.
Clock speed alone neither initializes the register nor blocks its effects.
Known valid/control state must prevent every meaningful use until the unreset data is initialized.
platform-physical-scan-test-coverage: Stuck-at fault coverage is not a percentage of correctly executed programs.
The percentage describes detected faults within the declared stuck-at model, denominator and test assumptions.
Stuck-at coverage alone does not establish at-speed timing correctness.
Undetected defects can fall outside the stuck-at model and need not be packaging failures.
